correctness.rationale: Independently reconstructed the average-payoff formula from incidence multiplicities and its iff converse by every one-cooperator test. Verified that the normalized payoff gap equals r(v-g)/(v-1)-1 and determines the direction of every possible update, with positive chance of progress from each mixed state due to positive pair multiplicity. Derived the complete-hypergraph pure-birth and pure-death probabilities by counting incident edge samples and exact geometric holding times. Checked both boundary harmonic contributions give g/(g-1) v log v. Recomputed the Fano-plane 12-vs-9 incidence counts and resulting 4/7 vs 3/7 rates. The actual standalone exact rational program successfully tested all Fano states, all binary configurations on six complete designs, harmonic formulas and non-proving asymptotic sanity; finite tests do not replace analytic general proof. Critical limitations: regularity, constant returns, highest-earner rule, no mutation, single focal-player time unit.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Wei 2026 supplies the elementary imitation protocol and numerically explores changing resource states; it does not state any 2-design if-and-only-if or an exact all-initial-state threshold. Alvarez 2021 supplies a dense well-mixed replicator limit with critical synergy asymptotically one; the finite threshold (v-1)/(v-g) converges to one, so the new theorem is consistent but is not an immediate corollary of an asymptotic population limit. Wang–Su 2026 conditions rely on different stochastic updating and weak selection; they do not force a strict monotone strategy count under the current rule. Liu--Masuda 2023 has group-wide replacement and constant type fitness, with different transition probabilities, so it does not imply the best-earner payoff-incidence criterion. The Fano example shows the stronger opposite-to-naive-lumpability fact despite balanced payoff gaps. No materially inspected source implies all parts of the package; specialized uninspected work could.

originality.rationale: The closest primary studies introduce the same hypergraph payoff/imitation mechanism, a mean-field large-population approximation, or weak-selection network methods, but the source statements inspected do not imply the conjunction of the finite all-configuration design iff, strict sharp global fixation on every 2-design, exact complete-hypergraph takeover time, and Fano geometric non-lumpability. The balanced-design identity, replicator limiting threshold and elementary birth-chain waiting-time calculation are classical tools and not separately claimed new. Direct exact implication comparison, original full texts and relevant accessible historical claims were used. Broader uninspected literature and separate supplementary results are genuine priority risks.
residual_risks: The 2021 paper points to supplementary replicator details not separately inspected here; the presently reviewed main text is not enough to exclude every possible finite-result corollary there.
A specialized study of balanced block designs and higher-order imitation may contain equivalent finite statements despite no such match in actual targeted searches.
Historical priority has not been independently validated; the label PASS is a self-review reasoned assessment, not certification.

value.rationale: The target is the natural all-configuration strong-selection takeover question for public-goods hypergraph evolution introduced in the primary recent source. The theorem identifies exactly when regular incidence forces identical payoff by strategy, yields a sharp all-population fixation threshold valid even on sparse nonsymmetric block systems, determines finite expected absorption and the correct two-boundary v log v constant on the full design, and shows by a sharp Fano witness that equal payoff by strategy does not imply count-Markov behavior. These distinctions support when mean-field reductions can and cannot be used for waiting-time predictions. The finding is not an arbitrary finite re-computation; Fano is the smallest symmetric 2-(v,3,1) projective plane providing a natural geometry contrast.
